title: Pause on the impression
idea: We are upset less by events than by the judgments we add to them. Between what happens and your reaction, there is a gap.
apply: When something stings, say: this is an impression, not yet the truth. Then ask what actually happened.
remind: Pause. Separate the event from the story.
who: Tom, whose boss replies with one word.

msgs.x: Here is the report you asked for.

scenes.nar: Tom sends his boss a report. The reply is a single word. Fine.

msgs.x: I am about to be let go.

scenes.nar: His mind races. She is angry. I am about to be let go. In minutes, one word has become a disaster.
Then he remembers Epictetus. This is an impression, not yet the truth. What actually happened? She wrote one word.
He simply asks if she wants any changes. She says it was great. He saved himself an evening of worry.
